-# How it works
 
-As of 2022-11, the way coverstore works is that new covers that are uploaded to Open Library go into `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/localdisk/` within a directory named `/YYYY/MM/DD/`. A record for each cover (and its size variants) is recorded within the `cover` table of the `coverstore` psql db located on `ol-db1`.
+The database columns describe the location and status:
 
-At some (presumably advantageous if) regular interval, as the `localdisk` fills, the files can undergo archival, a process whereby covers are compressed and bundled into tar archives which are moved into the `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` directory within folders called "staging items" (e.g. `covers_0007`). The database reference to these covers' filename paths are updated accordingly by the `archive.py` script.
+| `archived` | `uploaded` | `failed` | `filename*` |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| false | false | false | Source paths relative to `data_root/localdisk` |
+| true | false | false | Source paths still served locally; zip files staged under `items` |
+| true | true | false | Verified direct archive.org zip-entry URLs |
+| false | false | true | At least one required local image is missing; operator action needed |
 
-Mek speculates that when coverstore attempts to look up a cover, its entry is looked up in the DB and if the filename is a tar, coverstore first looks on disk for a "staging item" folder within the staging directory `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` and if no such "staging item" exists, the staging item is assumed to have been uploaded as an archive.org item having the same name (and thus redirects/resolves its request via archive.org).  
+`archive.archive(test=False)` stages up to 10,000 eligible covers, placing all four variants in zip files. It marks a cover `archived` only after the zip files close successfully. `archive.archive()` is a dry run. A missing source marks that cover `failed` and leaves its paths untouched. A retry checks existing zip entries and rejects different content under the same name.
 
-# State of Cover Archival
+After staging, call `Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True, test=False)`. Upload starts only when a newer cover ID has closed the batch's 10,000-ID range, all non-failed covers in it have been staged, and all four local zips contain the expected entries. The method validates local zip CRCs, sends each local zip through the `ia` CLI (including retries where the remote name already exists), verifies the **exact** filename in all four archive.org items, and then updates every staged non-failed cover in the batch to direct remote URLs with `uploaded=true`. It removes local source files and zip files after the database transaction commits. Source cleanup is recorded in `items/.locks/*.sources.json` so a retry can finish it after an interruption. If the upload is incomplete, it raises `UploadIncompleteError`; the database remains local and a retry is safe. `test=True` checks status without uploading, updating the database, or deleting files. Operators can call `process_pending(upload=False, finalize=True, test=False)` after an out-of-band upload; they must ensure the remote zip content matches the local staged zip.
 
-As of 2022-11 there are 5,692,598 unarchived covers on `ol-covers0` and we're starting to run short on space. Specifically, cover archives haven't been happening since ~2014-11-29, as we can see from the following brutally slow query:
+Staging and completion take an exclusive, nonblocking lock in `data_root/items/.locks/` for the 10,000-ID batch. Conflicting jobs raise `BatchBusyError`. The lock directory must be on shared storage when multiple coverserver hosts run archival jobs.

-In the previous query, we see that the last cover (id #7,315,539) was archived on `2014-11-29` and resides within a tar `covers_0007_31.tar`. Coverstore assumes this tar resolves to an `item` folder called `covers_0007`, either staged on disk within `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` or on archive.org/details/covers_0007. In this case, at the time of writing, this item was still staged on disk. As far as Mek can tell, staged items presumably get manually uploaded to archive.org under an item having the same name.

-The item name itself (e.g. `coverd_0007`) is a combination of the prefix `covers` and the code `web.numify("%010d.jpg" % cover.id)[:4]` where, in this case, `cover.id` is `7315539`. The `"%010d"` format parameter pads the `cover.id` with leading 0's until it is 10 digits long and then the [:4] takes the first 4 digits of this padded number. Anything lower than `cover.id` 1,000,000 will thus be in `covers_0000` and from there the next 1M will be in `covers_0002` and so on. In total, this scheme allows for just under 10B covers before it breaks, which is a sufficiently unlikely number to hit!

+def test_stage_validate_and_finalize_closed_batch(archive_db, tmp_path):
+    FakeUploader.uploaded = set()
+    image_names = {
+        'filename': 'a.jpg', 'filename_s': 'a-S.jpg',
+        'filename_m': 'a-M.jpg', 'filename_l': 'a-L.jpg',
+    }
+    for name in image_names.values():
+        (tmp_path / 'localdisk' / name).write_bytes(name.encode())
+    archive_db.insert(
+        'cover', id=8_000_123, archived=False, failed=False, uploaded=False,
+        **image_names,
+    )
+    archive_db.insert(
+        'cover', id=8_000_124, archived=False, failed=False, uploaded=False,
+        filename='missing.jpg', filename_s='missing-S.jpg',
+        filename_m='missing-M.jpg', filename_l='missing-L.jpg',
+    )
+
+    assert archive.archive(test=True) == 1
+    assert archive.archive(test=False) == 1
+    assert archive.archive(test=False) == 0
+
+    row = archive_db.select('cover', where='id=8000123')[0]
+    failed_row = archive_db.select('cover', where='id=8000124')[0]
+    assert row.archived
+    assert not row.uploaded
+    assert row.filename == 'a.jpg'
+    assert failed_row.failed
+    assert not failed_row.archived
+    for size in archive.SIZES:
+        path = archive.Batch.get_abspath(8, 0, size)
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
+            assert zf.compression == zipfile.ZIP_STORED
+            assert zf.namelist() == [archive.Cover(row).entry_name(size)]
+        assert archive.count_files_in_zip(path) == 1
+
+    batch = archive.Batch(8, 0)
+    with pytest.raises(archive.UploadIncompleteError, match='still open'):
+        batch.process_pending(upload=True, test=False, uploader=FakeUploader)
+    assert not FakeUploader.uploaded
+
+    # A later ID closes the 10k range. It is already complete and is not staged.
+    archive_db.insert('cover', id=8_010_000, archived=True, failed=False, uploaded=True)
+    for size in ('', 's', 'm'):
+        FakeUploader.uploaded.add((batch.item_name(size), batch.zip_filename(size)))
+    with pytest.raises(archive.UploadIncompleteError, match='l_covers_0008_00.zip'):
+        batch.process_pending(finalize=True, test=False, uploader=FakeUploader)
+    assert not archive_db.select('cover', where='id=8000123')[0].uploaded
+    assert (tmp_path / 'localdisk' / 'a.jpg').exists()
+
+    statuses = batch.process_pending(
+        upload=True, finalize=True, test=False, uploader=FakeUploader
+    )
+    assert statuses['completed'] == 1
+    assert all(statuses[size]['uploaded'] for size in archive.SIZES)
+    row = archive_db.select('cover', where='id=8000123')[0]
+    assert row.archived
+    assert row.uploaded
+    for size in archive.SIZES:
+        key = f'filename_{size}' if size else 'filename'
+        assert row[key] == archive.Cover.get_cover_url(row.id, size)
+        assert not os.path.exists(archive.Batch.get_abspath(8, 0, size))
+    assert not (tmp_path / 'localdisk' / 'a.jpg').exists()
+    assert archive_db.select('cover', where='id=8000124')[0].filename == 'missing.jpg'
+
+    response = code.app.request('/b/id/8000123-S.jpg')
+    assert response.status.startswith('302')
+    assert response.headers['Location'] == row.filename_s
+    assert batch.process_pending(finalize=True, test=False, uploader=FakeUploader)[
+        'completed'
+    ] == 0

+def test_zip_retry_rejects_changed_content(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

+    manager.close()
+    assert archive.count_files_in_zip(archive.Batch.get_abspath(8, 0)) == 1

+    FakeUploader.uploaded = {

+
+    original_remove = os.remove

+    assert batch.process_pending(finalize=True, test=False, uploader=FakeUploader)[
+        'completed'
+    ] == 0
+    assert not os.path.exists(batch.source_manifest)
